name: Organimi
tagline: Builds interactive org charts, directories and photo boards from spreadsheet or HR system data.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: An org chart is a tree drawn from a CSV, and drawing trees is one of the most solved problems in software. An agent given a hierarchy library and a print stylesheet will get you node cards with photos, collapsible branches, search, and a PDF export in a single sitting. What Organimi sells on top of that is HRIS sync, shareable read-only links for people who will never install anything, and the comfort of not storing employee data in a script someone wrote on a Tuesday. If your chart is under a few hundred people and lives in a spreadsheet you already maintain, the SaaS is doing very little you cannot do yourself. If it needs to auto-refresh from your payroll system and be viewed by the whole company, it is doing quite a lot.
coreLoopDIY: Import a CSV of people and manager IDs, render a zoomable collapsible org chart with photos and search, and export it to PNG or print-ready PDF.
requirements: A CSV or spreadsheet of employees with a manager reference column
Optional photo files or image URLs
whatYouLose: HRIS and directory sync, so every change is a manual re-import
Public share links and view permissions for people who will not run a dev server
Matrix and dotted-line reporting, legends, and the fiddlier chart layouts
Hosted storage of employee data with someone else's security posture and DPA
Polish: pagination for huge charts, clean multi-page printing, mobile layout
moatNotes: The chart is trivial. Keeping it accurate without a human retyping it is the product, and that means connectors into HR systems nobody enjoys integrating with.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the chart is never the work. Keeping it current is the work, and that means a connector to the HR system, a link the CFO can open on a phone, and a vendor to point at when someone asks where employee photos and titles are stored. A local build handles a snapshot beautifully and handles the ongoing maintenance not at all, which is exactly the part companies were paying to avoid.
notes: Fine one-shot for a snapshot chart, bad one-shot for a living one.
prompt:
Build a local-only org chart viewer and editor. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, d3-hierarchy for layout, react-zoom-pan-pinch for canvas navigation, PapaParse for CSV, html-to-image for export. Data persists to IndexedDB via idb-keyval. Everything runs in the browser.

In scope:
1. CSV import screen with drag and drop. Expected columns: id, name, title, department, email, managerId, photoUrl. Let the user map arbitrary column headers to those fields before importing.
2. Build the tree from managerId. Detect and report cycles, orphans, and multiple roots instead of crashing. Show a validation summary the user can dismiss or fix.
3. Render a top-down org chart with rounded node cards: photo (fallback to initials avatar), name, title, department chip. Elbow connector lines between parent and children.
4. Collapse and expand any subtree by clicking a chevron on the node. Show a count of hidden descendants on collapsed nodes.
5. Zoom, pan, fit-to-screen, and a zoom percentage readout.
6. Search box that filters by name, title, or department, auto-expands ancestors of matches, and highlights hits.
7. Click a node to open a side panel for editing all fields, reassigning the manager via a searchable select, adding a direct report, or deleting the node (children reparent to the deleted node's manager).
8. Department color coding with a toggleable legend.
9. Export: PNG of the current chart, JSON of the full dataset, and CSV round-trip. Plus a print stylesheet that renders the expanded chart landscape on paper.
10. Seed the app with a 25-person sample org so it is usable immediately with no file.

Out of scope, do not build: authentication, multi-user editing, share links, HRIS integrations, dotted-line or matrix reporting, mobile-specific layout.

Use .env only if you add an optional image proxy; there are no other secrets. Ship a README with run instructions, the expected CSV schema, and one paragraph noting that all employee data stays in the browser's IndexedDB and is wiped by clearing site data.
